newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News -Oct 17.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News -Oct 17.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

In an effort to make its A$19 billion megabank deal more attractive to investors, the Queensland Government yesterday released a package of sweeteners, including a promise to forgo dividends on some of its shares for three years and the offer of "loyalty options" which will give investors who hold shares on December 1, 1998 the right to buy more shares at A$5.00 as the Government sells down its own stake. Page 1.

According to the Reserve Bank's quarterly economic report, released yesterday, another interest rate reduction could be possible this year as long as wage claims are reined in. With the release of average weekly earnings figures for the three months to Agust due next week, evidence of moderation of wage growth could increase the odds of an early rate cut. Page 1.

The Australian Taxation Office boosted tax revenue by 11.7 per cent to A$98.6 billion for the year to June 1996, according to the ATO's annual report, tabled in Parliament yesterday, but net tax collections were still 2.3 per cent lower than last year's Budget forecasts. Page 3.

Addressing the McIntosh Securities investment seminar in New York overnight, Foster's Brewing Group chief executive Ted Kunkel said Foster's hoped to double the annual earnings contribution from Mildara Blass to A$100 million during the next five years and indicated that the brewer was placed to mount a major acquisition in the wine and beer sectors. Page 23.

Reflecting the strategy of the giant UK-based Barclays Group to emphasise asset management, BZW Investment Management chief executive officer Richard Douglas said yesterday that BZWIM would change its investment style and move out of direct property invesment through the sale of its half share in the trust management company for the BZW-Mirvac Property Funds. Page 23.

A paper produced by the Australian Institute of Company Directors suggests that directors should keep a complete set of board papers, even after they retire from the board, in case they are later sued by the company or other parties. However, the paper concedes that directors who retain documents may not be able to use them if the company successfully claims they are subject to professional legal privilege. Page 23.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Yesterday's comments by the Reserve Bank in its quarterly report on the economy strongly indicated that an interest rate cut was unlikely unless the bank sees signs of moderating pressures on enterprise bargains. The comments will upset financial markets believing a rate cut this calendar year was inevitable following the release of last week's employment figures. Page 23.

Just two days after Australis Media Ltd shareholders approved resolutions clearing the pay TV operator's lifesaving US$150 million bond issue in the US, Australis managing director Neil Gamble was confirmed as the new chief executive of Sydney Harbour Casino Ltd. Page 23.

In a memorandum of understanding signed by Richard Pratt and New South Wales Premier Bob Carr, Pratt's Visy Industries has pledged to invest A$310 million in a packaging paper mill in southern New South Wales capable of producing 180,000 tonnes of brown pper annually from 600,000 tonnes of woodchips. Page 23.

The Queensland Government yesterday unveiled an attractive inducement package for its proposed bancassurance merger, comprising a forecast fully franked dividend yield of 9.2 per cent for the 1997, 1998 and 1999 financial years, plus a 1-for-2 entitlement to a portion of the Government's 70 per cent holding at A$5 a share in two years. Following the announcement, Metway Bank Ltd's share price rose three per cent above the Government's offer of A$4.80. Page 25.

Speaking to shareholders at Crown Ltd's annual meeting in Melbourne yesterday, chairman Lloyd Williams said the company would boost its marketing efforts to attract high-rolling investors from Asia and expected to produce first-quarter earnings slightly ahead of the previous period. Page 25.

BHP Minerals has sold its 20 per cent stake in Sun Prospecting & Mining, or Sungold, to South African joint venture partner and operator Anglovaal for A$60 million, reaping a A$45 million profit. Sungold was part of a package of assets bought by BHP in 184 in the acquisition of Utah International Inc. Page 25.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

The Queensland Government yesterday released details of a range of sweeteners to entice Metway Bank shareholders to accept its mega-bank proposal along with an independent expert's valuation of the proposal to merge Metway with the State-owned Suncorp insrance company and Queensland Industry Development Corp into a A$20 billion financial conglomerate. Page 25.

In its September quarter economic review, the Reserve Bank of Australia said its response to excessive wage demands was to hold monetary policy "firmer than otherwise to maintain the two to three per cent inflation objective", ruling out a lowering of intrest rates for the time being. Page 25.

Seven months after Andre Hilliou unexpectedly resigned from Sydney Harbour Casino, Australis Media managing director Neil Gamble was yesterday announced as the new chief executive. Australis has installed chief operating officer Larry Carleton as interim chief executive officer until a permanent replacement is found. Page 25.

Following profit forecast downgradings by media analysts, John Fairfax Holdings' finance director John Greaves said yesterday that a drop in advertising volumes and higher costs looked likely to force the newspaper group's first-quarter profit down by up to 25 per cent. Page 27.

Predicting tough trading conditions during 1996-97, Qantas said in its annual report released yesterday, that management would have to speed up the airline's ambitious cost-cutting program or face a disappointing result. Cost reduction targets have been increased from A$230 million to A$330 million to compensate for a prediction of lower revenue growth. Page 27.

The Lorna Hodgkinson Sunshine Nursing Home yesterday commenced talks with Dianne Davidson in an effort to recover some of the A$5 million defrauded over 20 years by her husband, former Sunshine financial controller, William Davidson. Davidson is serving three-year nine-month jail terms for defrauding the home and the staff superannuation fund of A$1.88 million. Page 27.
THE AGE

Crown Casino will open marketing offices in Beijing, Taipei and Kuala Lumpur later this year and an office in Shanghai next year as part of plans, announced by Crown chairman Lloyd Williams yesterday, to lure high-roller Asian gamblers to Australia. Willams said Crown's new Melbourne Southbank complex would be a showcase for Asian gamblers as it would be the best casino complex in the world. Page C1.

The Reserve Bank yesterday dashed hopes for another interest rate cut this year, saying a cut could create inflationary problems if wage demands continued to mount. However, the bank said if September quarter figures for wages growth remained within the bank's parameters, a last-minute change of mind could not be ruled out. Page C1.

Sydney Harbour Casino yesterday announced the appointment of Australis Media managing director Neil Gamble as the casino's new chief executive, after the announcement was delayed for 11 weeks as the New South Wales Gaming Authority conducted the necessary probity checks. Page C1.

Metway Bank shares soared to A$4.95 yesterday, following the Queensland Government's release of a package of inducements to attract investors to its megabank proposal and the release of an independent expert's valuation of the merger of Metway, State-owne Suncorp insurance company and Queensland Industry Development Corp. Page C1.

Canada's Bre-X Minerals has accused Perth-based explorer Golden Valley Mines NL of making "false and misleading" claims in its announcements of technical and finance agreements with Indonesian company PT Krueng Gasui (KG). KG holds an interest in a jointventure which contains part of the Busang gold deposit - the East Kalimantan deposit found by Bre-X. Page C3.

Dismissing local industry fears that it is poised to take on the Australian telephony market, US giant American Telephone & Telegraph Company says it has no plans to compete with Telstra or Optus when Australia's telephony market opens up to competition nxt year. Page C3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
